question: In Opinion 04/2023 concerning the Commission’s amended proposal for a Council Regulation on the methods and procedure for making available own resources, the European Court of Auditors (ECA) studied the Commission proposal, which ‘was expected to provide an average of up to €17 billion annually for the EU budget, and to help finance the expected budgetary expenditure for the repayment of NGEU and for the Social Climate Fund (SCF)’.

While the ECA opinion is generally positive, it does note that ‘the information available would not allow us to assess whether the expected annual revenues generated from the adjusted package for the next generation of own resources are, as intended, sufficient to cover the financial needs for both NGEU and the SCF’.

The ECA also points out that the Commission should have ‘inspection powers (including on-the-spot visits to national authorities) to complement the national controls that are needed to ensure that the own resource is properly calculated and collected.’ 1.
How has the Commission reacted to the ECA recommendations to complement the ‘available information’?
Does the Commission intend to seek the ‘inspection powers’ suggested by the ECA?
answer: On 20 June 2023, the Commission revised its proposal on the introduction of new own resources (1). The final package contains a contribution from the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), from the Emission Trading Scheme (ETS) and a statistical contribution linked to company profits.

The objective is to generate revenue that can repay a significant proportion of borrowing contracted to finance grants under the NextGenerationEU recovery plan. Nevertheless, borrowing will be repaid by the EU budget in any event, including if the Commission’s proposal is not adopted.

The primary objective of the package is to generate sufficient revenue to maintain the budget at an acceptable level, while at the same time limiting the Member States’ contribution calculated as a fixed percentage of their gross national income (GNI). The Commission attaches particular importance to the inspection of own resources, in order to guarantee equal treatment of Member States.

However, it considers that inspections have to be proportionate and tailored to the characteristics of each own resource and the risks involved. As regards the CBAM, to which the opinion of the Court of Auditors refers, the sectoral legislation eventually adopted by the co-legislator now gives the Commission inspection powers.

The Commission has taken these changes into account and has consequently adapted the CBAM own resource control mechanisms in its revised proposal. It thus considers the current mechanisms to be sufficient.
